events.summary: The U.S. Treasury has announced it will double its maximum bond buybacks for long-dated bonds from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation, effective September 9. This move targets bonds maturing in 10-20 years and 20-30 years to improve market liquidity, as long-term yields have reached near two-decade highs. While buybacks can enhance liquidity by allowing investors a predictable exit for older securities, they cannot fix the underlying issue of the national deficit.
events.title: Treasury Just Doubled Its Bond Buybacks: What That Can and Can't Fix

events.summary: Shares of several aerospace companies, including Curtiss-Wright, Redwire, Rocket Lab, Astronics, and Woodward, fell following news of surging oil prices and rising long-term interest rates. These factors are expected to increase operating and financing costs for airlines, leading to potential delays in fleet upgrades and maintenance, thus impacting aerospace manufacturers.

events.summary: The U.S. Treasury announced it will double the size of its liquidity support buyback operations for longer-dated nominal coupon securities from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation, effective September 9, 2026.
